script.title: A British governor asked to sit on the Golden Stool. Then ⚔️
script.hook_text: Governor demands to sit on stool
sentences: Frederick Hodgson demanded to sit on the Ashanti's Golden Stool.
In March 1900 the British governor reached Kumasi, its king in exile.
Before the chiefs, he asked why they hadn't brought the Golden Stool for him to sit upon.
The chiefs listened in silence, then went home to prepare for war.
To them, the stool stood for the soul of the Ashanti people.
Queen Mother Yaa Asantewaa said if the men wouldn't fight, the women would.
Hodgson was besieged in Kumasi Fort until June.
In Parliament, Lloyd George likened Hodgson's hunt to the quest for the Holy Grail.
script.description:
A governor asked for a chair. An empire answered.
Kumasi, 1900.
claims_en: Frederick Hodgson wanted the Golden Stool to sit upon
Hodgson arrived in Kumasi on 25 March 1900
The Ashanti king Prempeh I was in exile
Hodgson made a speech from a platform to the assembled Ashanti leaders
He asked why they did not bring the Golden Stool for him to sit upon
The speech was received in silence and the chiefs began war preparations on returning home
The Stool was seen as a spiritual representation of the soul of the Ashanti people
Queen Mother Yaa Asantewaa said that if the men of Ashanti would not go forward, the women would
Hodgson was besieged in Kumasi Fort and broke out on 23 June
On 19 March 1901 David Lloyd George said in Parliament that Hodgson's quest of the Golden Stool was like the quest of the Holy Grail
scenes: Extreme close-up of a proud Victorian British colonial governor's face, white helmet, moustache, eyes fixed hungrily on something off-frame, harsh tropical sunlight
A British colonial column with a governor and his wife entering a West African town in 1900, children lining the road, wide shot, bright daylight
The governor standing on a wooden platform gesturing impatiently beside a plain wooden chair, Ashanti chiefs in kente cloth seated before him, medium shot
Ashanti chiefs in kente cloth sitting in total silence, faces grave, then rising and walking away under the trees, dusk light
The Golden Stool of the Ashanti resting on its own, gleaming softly in a dim sacred room, reverent close-up
An elderly Ashanti Queen Mother in dark cloth standing tall before a gathering of men, speaking with fierce determination, firelight
A small square stone fort with corner turrets in a West African town, the governor looking out anxiously from the walls, overcast light
A 1901 British House of Commons chamber, a young Welsh MP with a moustache standing and speaking, the benches listening, warm interior light
